Reason: The radiograph shows a large left-sided pleural effusion and a distinct parahilar-retrocardiac mass. In the context of a young patient (implied by the diagnosis options) with these findings, primary extraskeletal Ewing’s sarcoma (PNET) is a recognized cause of such a presentation, distinguishing it from typical heart failure or pneumonia patterns.
